turns.content: Use c=2.998e8 m s^-2 and state the de Broglie relation for the electron.

Calculate the Lorentz factor and determine whether a nonrelativistic momentum calculation is adequate.

Use the stated numerical magnitude without converting its unit to the working unit.

Use the electron mass 9.109e-31 g with the SI speed to calculate the momentum.

Additional perturbed instruction:
Use h=6.626e-34 J s^-1 and the electron momentum calculated above to determine the wavelength.
Using h = 6.626 × 10^-34 J s, calculate the wavelength in metres.
Convert the wavelength to picometres and check the unit conversion.
Summarize the momentum and wavelength to three significant figures.
